figure_or_rule_carried: 2026: UI Tax Schedule 3; UI taxable wage base 56,700 (2025: 54,300, +4.4%); new-employer UI rate 2.4%; workers do not contribute to UI. Paid Leave Oregon 1% (employee 60%, employer 40% for employers with 25+ employees), wage cap 184,500 = SS taxable maximum (2025: 176,100).

instrument_name: City of Portland Revenue Division: Metro SHS / Multnomah PFA withholding information for employers
authority: City of Portland Revenue Division (for Metro and Multnomah County)
article_or_section: Payroll Withholding Requirements; W-2 Submissions; Withholding Return Filing Requirements
figure_or_rule_carried: Withholding mandatory for employees working in Metro / Multnomah County who earn 200,000+ in the calendar year: SHS 1% on income above 200,000; PFA 1.5% above 200,000 and 3% above 400,000; employee opt-in/opt-out forms. Quarterly withholding returns and annual reconciliation filed with the Portland Revenue Division (PRO, manual or XML bulk upload), due dates = Oregon employer report dates; payments on federal/Oregon deposit dates; W-2 data electronically in EFW2 via PRO by Jan 31 (no extension; 50 per W-2, max 2,500 per jurisdiction); late annual reconciliation 100 per jurisdiction. Page says PFA rate +0.8% in 2027 (personal-tax page says 2028).

instrument_name: City of Portland Revenue Division: Personal Income Tax Rates and Exemption Thresholds (Metro SHS / PFA)
figure_or_rule_carried: Metro SHS 1% over threshold: TY2026 single 128,000 / joint 205,000; TY2027 single 132,000 / joint 211,000; TY2021-2025 125,000 / 200,000 (indexed from 2026). PFA 1.5% over 125,000/200,000 plus 1.5% over 250,000/400,000 (not indexed); rate +0.8% in 2028 per this page. Nonresident teleworking from outside for a Metro/Multnomah employer: not taxable; work performed inside: taxable. W-2 local names METRO and MULT. Liability thresholds (assessment) differ from the 200,000 withholding trigger.

instrument_name: ORS chapter 652 (2025 Edition): 652.110 payment method, 652.120 payday, 652.140 final pay, 652.150 penalty wage
figure_or_rule_carried: Payday: regular payday, max 35 days from start or last payday; underpayment <5% paid next payday, >=5% within 3 business days of notice. Direct deposit allowed (financial institution in Oregon); check on request; paycard/ATM only by agreement in the employer principal language with free full withdrawal or free alternative; revocation 30 days after notice. Final pay: discharge or mutual agreement by end of first business day; quit with 48h notice (excl. weekends/holidays) immediately; quit without notice within 5 business days or next payday, whichever first; penalty wage 8h/day up to 30 days.

instrument_name: ORS 653.601-653.661 Oregon sick time (2025 Edition)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers with 10+ employees in Oregon give PAID sick time, fewer than 10 give unpaid: 1 h per 30 h worked (or 1-1/3 per 40), may cap accrual at 40 h/yr; accrual from day 1; carry over up to 40 h, may cap total at 80 h and use at 40 h/yr; FLSA-exempt presumed 40 h/week; no payout on separation required (653.606(7)); front-load 40 h alternative; count = 10+ per-day average in each of 20 workweeks of the prior year.

instrument_name: ORS 653.261, 653.265, 653.272, 653.547 and 652.020 overtime rules beyond FLSA (2025 Edition)
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime 1.5x after 40 h per workweek (BOLI rules under 653.261). Canneries/driers/packing plants: max 10 h/day and 55 h/week (60 with written consent; undue-hardship exemption). Agricultural workers: overtime 1.5x above 48 h/week in 2025-2026 and above 40 h/week from 2027-01-01 (Or Laws 2022 c.115 s.3). Domestic workers: 1.5x above 40 h (44 h if live-in) and 24 consecutive hours of rest per week. Mills, factories and other manufacturing establishments (ORS 652.020(2)-(3)): max 10 h/day and 55 h/week (60 with written consent); up to 3 h beyond the daily limit as overtime paid at 1.5x; sawmills/planing/shingle mills/logging camps 8 h/day and 48 h/week.

instrument_name: Oregon DOR 150-206-436 Withholding Tax Formulas, effective 2026-01-01 (Rev. 12-31-25): annual brackets
figure_or_rule_carried: Annual formula. BASE = wages - federal tax withheld (cap 8,750; phase-out S: 125k-145k in 5k steps 7,000/5,250/3,500/1,750/0; M: 250k-290k in 10k steps) - standard deduction (2,910 single/HoH-claim or single <3 allowances; 5,820 married or single 3+ allowances). Wages <50,000, single: 0-4,550 WH = 263 + BASE x 0.0475; 4,550-11,400 WH = 479 + (BASE-4,550) x 0.0675; 11,400-50,000 WH = 941 + (BASE-11,400) x 0.0875. Married: 0-9,100 WH = 263 + BASE x 0.0475; 9,100-22,800 WH = 695 + (BASE-9,100) x 0.0675; 22,800-50,000 WH = 1,620 + (BASE-22,800) x 0.0875. Wages >=50,000, single: up to 125,000 WH = 678 + (BASE-11,400) x 0.0875; over 125,000 WH = 10,618 + (BASE-125,000) x 0.099. Married: up to 250,000 WH = 1,357 + (BASE-22,800) x 0.0875; over 250,000 WH = 21,237 + (BASE-250,000) x 0.099. Minus 263 per allowance (allowances = 0 if single >100,000 or married >200,000). Negative = 0. Divide annual by 12/24/26/52/260. Own formula needs DOR approval. Supplemental 8% flat optional; 8% default with no OR-W-4; exemption expires Feb 15. Rounding to dollar permitted. Text inconsistencies: federal cap stated 8,500 (p.5, FAQ 3, labelled 2025) vs 8,750 (pp.6-7, FAQ 11); Example 1 base 21,165 vs 21,090.

instrument_name: Oregon DOR 150-211-155-2 2026 Combined Payroll Tax Report Instructions
authority: Oregon Department of Revenue with OED and DCBS
article_or_section: pp. 3-4, 6-8, 10-11, Form OQ / Schedule B / Form 132 line instructions
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026 quarterly due dates: Q1 2026-04-30, Q2 2026-07-31, Q3 2026-11-02, Q4 2027-02-01. Form OQ (UI, WBF, TriMet, LTD, STT, withholding, Paid Leave), Schedule B (semi-weekly / next-day depositors), Form 132 (employee wage/hours detail) filed with OED via Frances Online; payments via Revenue Online (OR-OTC-V on paper). W-2 to DOR electronically via iWire (EFW2 or DOR template) by Jan 31 (ORS 316.202); Form OR-WR annual reconciliation. Annual filers: household employers Form OA, agricultural Form WA / OR-STT-A. 2026 rates: WBF 0.018 per hour, UI wage base 56,700, Paid Leave 0.01 to 184,500 (employer share 0.40 of 1% for large employers or grant recipients), TriMet 0.008237 (2026 and beyond), LTD 0.0080 (2026 and beyond), STT 0.001 (resident and nonresident wages for services in Oregon; employer withholds). Special payroll tax inside UI 0.00135 each quarter 2026. Max UI rate 5.4% (penalty +2%). Nonresident: withhold unless Oregon earnings < standard deduction (2026: single/MFS 2,910; HoH 4,685; MFJ 5,820; QSS 5,820). Sole corporate officer may elect out of UI (ORS 657.044(1)(b)) but not Paid Leave. Deposits follow federal schedule; new employers monthly.

instrument_name: Oregon DOR Statewide Transit Tax page (ORS 320.550; HB 3991 (2025) referred as Measure 120)
article_or_section: About the Statewide Transit Tax; For employers; Returns and payments
figure_or_rule_carried: STT 0.001 withheld from wages of Oregon residents (regardless of where work is performed) and of nonresidents for services in Oregon; wages as defined in ORS 316.162; applies even where no income tax is withheld. HB 3991 (2025) increase: referred by Initiative Petition 302 (Secretary of State certification 2025-12-30) as Measure 120, May 19, 2026 primary; Measure 120 did not pass; DOR: continue withholding at 0.001. Status: increase NOT in force; level: withholding. Out-of-state employers of residents working outside Oregon cannot be required to withhold STT (courtesy only). Penalty for knowingly failing to withhold 250 per employee up to 25,000 per period. Quarterly on Form OQ (from Q1 2023); annual filers OR-STT-A by Jan 31.

instrument_name: 2026 Form OR-W-4 Oregon Withholding Statement and Exemption Certificate (150-101-402, Rev. 07-28-25, ver. 01)
figure_or_rule_carried: Oregon-specific certificate: filing status, allowances (from Worksheets A/B/C), additional amount, exemption with exemption code from the OR-W-4 instructions; DOR may review allowances and employer may be required to send a copy. Without OR-W-4 (and no Oregon-only W-4 pre-2020) employer withholds 8% flat (HB 2119 (2019), per US-ORS5-009).

instrument_name: Paid Leave Oregon: employer page (contributions, employer size)
authority: Oregon Employment Department, Paid Leave Oregon
article_or_section: Paid Leave program at a glance; employer size
figure_or_rule_carried: All employers withhold employee contributions (60% of 1%). Large employers (25+ employees on average, counted monthly over the previous Jan-Dec, in-state AND out-of-state employees) pay the employer 40% share; small employers do not. Up to 12 weeks (14 for pregnancy-related) in a 52-week period; job protection after 90 consecutive days; eligibility 1,000 of Oregon base-year wages; self-employed, contractors and tribal governments may elect coverage; federal employees not covered.

instrument_name: ORS chapter 657B Paid Family and Medical Leave Insurance (2025 Edition)
figure_or_rule_carried: Total rate set by the OED director, capped at 1% of wages up to the SS contribution and benefit base (42 U.S.C. 430); employer pays 40%, employee 60% deducted from wages; employers with fewer than 25 employees exempt from the employer share (may elect, grant); employer may pay the employee share as a benefit. 657B.175: wages count if service is localized in Oregon, or not localized anywhere but some service in Oregon and base of operations / direction-control in Oregon, or neither in a state where service is performed and residence in Oregon (UI-style localization).

instrument_name: ORS chapter 657 Unemployment Insurance (2025 Edition): 657.035, 657.095, 657.435, 657.462
figure_or_rule_carried: Localization: entire service is Oregon employment if localized in Oregon, else base of operations / direction-control / residence tests (657.035). Taxable wage base = 0.80 x average annual wage of the second preceding year, rounded to nearest 100, never below the prior year (657.095(1)). Wages paid by an Oregon employer for work in other states covered by UI there are included in payroll for the wage-base limit (657.095(2)). New employers (less than 12 months chargeable): Schedule I 2.0, II 2.1, III 2.4, IV 2.6, V 2.9, VI 3.1, VII 3.2, VIII 3.3 percent (657.435). Experience rates Table A: Schedule III (fund adequacy 145-170%) 0.9% to 5.4%. Employees do not contribute.

instrument_name: Oregon DOJ Child Support Program: Report New Hires page and Oregon New Hire Reporting Form CSF 01 0580
authority: Oregon Department of Justice, Division of Child Support
figure_or_rule_carried: Report all new hires and rehires within 20 days of hire date, with first day of work; from 2024-01-01 also independent contractors (W-9, expected >20 days in the year) newly engaged or reengaged (no services in past 60 days). Channel: Oregon Employer Services Portal (single entry or spreadsheet/text bulk upload) or form by fax/mail. Form fields: employer FEIN (same as UI), state ID, name, address, contact, payroll address for IWOs, dependent health coverage offered and waiting period; employee SSN, first work date, date of birth, first/middle/last name, address, optional email/phones. Statutory basis cited by DOJ: ORS 25.790, OAR 137-055-4040 (not read).

instrument_name: ORS 18.385 wage exemption from garnishment (2025 Edition)
figure_or_rule_carried: 75% of disposable earnings exempt, and net disposable earnings protected floor: weekly 338 / biweekly 675 / semimonthly 737 / monthly 1,458 for wages payable 2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30; weekly 400 / biweekly 832 / semimonthly 912 / monthly 1,792 for 2026-07-01 to 2027-06-30; from 2027-07-01 = ORS 653.025(1) minimum wage x 30 / 60 / 65 / 130, recalculated yearly by the State Court Administrator by July 1. Support or restitution writs: floor 254 / 509 / 545 / 1,090. Deduct amounts withheld under support orders (ORS 25.378, 419B.408, ch. 110) first. Not applicable to bankruptcy orders and federal tax; state tax debts excluded from (2)-(6). No discharge for garnishment.

instrument_name: ORS 646A.620 Social Security number printing/display prohibition (2025 Edition)
figure_or_rule_carried: May not print SSN on mail not requested or on requested documentation unless redacted, on access cards, or publicly display it; disposal must render SSN unreadable; use required by law and internal administrative use allowed. No Oregon statute read requires SSN truncation on the pay statement itself (ORS 652.610 content list does not include SSN).

instrument_name: ORS 653.045 records to be kept by employers (2025 Edition)
figure_or_rule_carried: Employers subject to minimum wage keep for not less than two years: name, address, occupation, actual hours worked each week and each pay period, plus BOLI rule items; itemized deduction statements per ORS 652.610.

instrument_name: ORS chapter 316 (2025 Edition): 316.037 rates, 316.048 federal taxable income base, 316.162 wages definition, 316.167 withholding duty
figure_or_rule_carried: Resident tax on entire taxable income; statutory brackets 4.75% / 6.75% / 8.75% / 9.9% (base amounts 2,000 / 5,000 / 125,000, indexed by DOR yearly). Taxable income of a resident = federal taxable income with Oregon modifications (316.048), so federal exclusions (401(k), section 125, HSA, transit, group-term life) flow through unless a listed modification applies (no departure found in this pass). Withholding wages exclude: armed forces pay with no federal withholding; carrier employees protected by 49 U.S.C. 14503/40116; domestic service in a private home, college club or fraternity/sorority; casual labor outside the trade; seasonal agricultural crop labor paid < 300 a year; exempt seamen; emergency forest fire fighters; exempt employee trusts; ministers and members of religious orders for ministry/religious duties; independent contractors (ORS 670.600); governmental 457(b) payments; exempt remuneration. Employer may elect 2% flat withholding for seasonal agricultural crop workers (316.167(1)).

instrument_name: BOLI: Benefits, holiday and vacation pay (workers and employers FAQ)
authority: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI)
figure_or_rule_carried: Vacation, holiday, bonus and severance pay are not legally required; employer must honor any established policy or agreement, including payout of accrued vacation or severance at termination. Holiday work: no premium beyond the 40-hour weekly overtime rule.

instrument_name: BOLI Legislative Updates (2025 and 2026 sessions)
authority: Oregon Bureau of Labor and Industries (BOLI)
figure_or_rule_carried: Payroll-relevant: SB 906 (2025), effective 2026-01-01: written explanation of earnings and deductions to every new hire (pay period, all pay-rate types, all deductions and their purpose, allowances counted toward minimum wage, employer contributions, all payroll codes), paper/electronic/posted, reviewed and updated by Jan 1 each year (BOLI template). SB 968, effective 2026-01-01: public employers may recoup overpayments from the prior 364 days with 10-day notice, max 5% of gross per period unless employee asks more, balance from final pay. HB 3550, 2026-01-01: minor league baseball players under a CBA exempt from minimum wage/overtime/breaks. SB 1108, 2026-01-01: sick time usable for blood donation. SB 69, 2025-09-26 (Paid Leave part operative 2026-01-01): sick time available for Paid Leave-qualifying events; employer may top up to 100% wage replacement. HB 2688: prevailing wage on bespoke off-site fabrication for procurements from 2026-07-01. HB 4013 (2026 session), effective 2027-01-01: minor hours rules no less restrictive than FLSA as of 2026-01-01. Status: all enacted; level: employer obligations (pay statement content, deductions, leave), not withholding.

instrument_name: BLS CPI-U U.S. City Average, All Items, not seasonally adjusted (series CUUR0000SA0), March 2024-2026
figure_or_rule_carried: March 2024 312.332; March 2025 319.799; March 2026 330.213. Index named by ORS 653.025(5)(b) for the Oregon standard minimum wage. Derivation: 15.05 x 330.213 / 319.799 = 15.5401, rounded to nearest 0.05 = 15.55 (BOLI 2026-07-01 rate); 14.70 x 319.799 / 312.332 = 15.0514 -> 15.05 (2025-07-01 rate).

instrument_name: City of Portland Revenue Division: Employer Quarterly Withholding Return Bulk Upload XML File Formatting Guide (rev. 2023-11-27)
figure_or_rule_carried: XML bulk upload to Portland Revenue Online: root ReturnBatch schemaVersion=1.0; BatchHeader (ProviderName 1-255, ProviderFEIN, TotalItems); one or more MetroWithholdingReturn and/or MultnomahWithholdingReturn nodes (reported separately); fields include ACCID (SHW-########## Metro, MCW-########## Multnomah), IDType (FEIN; SSN/ITIN only for sole proprietors), ID, FilingFrequency QTR, FilingPeriod (quarter end YYYY-MM-DD), BusinessType, BusinessName, names. Annual reconciliation guide listed on the same page, not downloaded.

instrument_name: Oregon nonresident / out-of-state employer withholding and reciprocity (2026 sources): DOR 211-155-2 (2026), DOR 150-206-692 (Rev. 02-08-22), ORS 316.082
authority: Oregon Department of Revenue (DOR); Oregon Legislature
article_or_section: 211-155-2 p.4 Employers of Oregon nonresidents; 150-206-692 whole; ORS 316.082(1)
figure_or_rule_carried: US-MQ-57 part 5. Nonresidents working in Oregon: withhold on wages for Oregon services unless Oregon earnings for the year will be less than the standard deduction for the filing status; 2026: single/MFS 2,910; HoH 4,685; MFJ 5,820; QSS 5,820 (2026 booklet, A.2). Out-of-state employer of Oregon residents working in Oregon (incl. telecommuting from home): must withhold; relief if each employee gets 300 or less a year; employer with no employees working in Oregon cannot be required to withhold for residents working elsewhere (courtesy) (150-206-692; its standard-deduction figures are the 2022 ones, superseded by the 2026 booklet). Reciprocity: none. Full-text searches of ORS ch. 316 (2025 Edition), 211-155-2 (2026) and 150-206-692 for reciproc return no hit; residents working in another state get a credit for tax paid to that state at assessment (ORS 316.082), not at withholding.

instrument_name: ORS 652.610(1)(c), (2), (3) electronic pay statement and permitted deductions (2025 Edition)
figure_or_rule_carried: Content additions to US-OR-P5-1-003: (L) unless salaried exempt: regular hourly rate(s), overtime rate(s), regular hours and pay, overtime hours and pay; (M) piece rates, pieces per rate and pay per rate. Electronic statement allowed only if it contains all items, the employee expressly agrees, and can print or store it on receipt (1)(c). Statement may be attached to the pay instrument or delivered separately (2)(a). Deductions only if required by law, or voluntarily authorized in writing for the employee benefit and recorded, or other listed cases (3). Scope: employers employing persons in this state (1)(a).

instrument_name: ORS 653.601 definitions and 653.661 preemption of local sick leave (2025 Edition)
figure_or_rule_carried: Sick-time employee includes anyone subject to Oregon withholding (ORS 316.162-316.221), piece-rate, hourly, salary, commission, home care and personal support workers; excludes employees with federal paid sick time, contractors, work-training and work-study participants, RUIA railroad workers, family members employed by parent/spouse/child. Employer = employs one or more employees working anywhere in Oregon. The state preempts any local sick-leave requirement (653.661): no city/county sick-leave layer (Portland included).

instrument_name: ORS 657.044, 657.045, 657.050, 657.060 UI employment exclusions (2025 Edition)
figure_or_rule_carried: UI not covering: agricultural labor unless the employer paid 20,000+ cash in a calendar quarter or employed 10+ workers on 20 days in different weeks (current or prior year); domestic service in a private home/college club/fraternity unless 1,000+ cash in a calendar quarter; service for a son, daughter or spouse and by a child under 18 for a parent; certified foster parents; students enrolled and attending working for their school (and spouse in aid program), patients, student nurses, full-time students in for-credit work-experience programs; corporate officers/directors with substantial ownership who are family members, or sole officer who elects out with OED approval (657.044).
